title: Beithir finds the cats' road in the snow
summary: A herder of the central mountains follows three strayed ewes into a high saddle and finds a line of prints worn into the frozen turf on both sides of it, running straight where the ground gave the beast no cause to turn; his own hearth's elders tell him their fathers knew the same line and the same two turns of year it is kept in.

title: The gatepost sign first cut
summary: A household of the high valleys cuts a fresh mark into its gatepost at the turn of year the cats' smell and track return to the passes, and scrapes it away again once both are gone, so that a stranger walking the crossing weeks can read the closed season on every post without asking what the mark means.

title: Àirighean a' Bhealaich stand empty
summary: The herders' summer camps on the high passes are found stripped and shuttered at the same point in every year while the cats cross, a boy sent up in error by his father's lost count of days finding one already closed and coming down again with nothing worse than a wasted night's walk.

title: Thirty head lost to a broken custom
summary: A herdsman of the lower slopes, trusting his own count of the year over his neighbours' gatepost signs, keeps his cattle ten days past the crossing's start and brings them down to find thirty head missing from the herd, torn on the ground above the track in a way no wolf of that country tears ground.

title: The cats turn back at the foothills
summary: A family watching from a rise above the track sees the crossing cats turn from the eastern passes and go back down toward the western foothills for no cause the watchers can find, and the country reads the plain sign as a warning rather than let it pass unanswered.

title: The households store double
summary: On the strength of the turning cats the country stores double against a hard winter that no other sign has yet shown, cutting peat and laying by grain and dried meat past what the ordinary count of mouths at each hearth calls for; the winter that follows proves hard enough to repay the extra carrying.

title: Word comes of a failed harvest inland
summary: Word reaches Teallaichean a' Chladaich that kin settled two valleys further into the hills than the shore's people commonly go have had their harvest fail badly enough that they will not see the winter through unhelped, and Cairbre resolves to lead ten of his own hearth up to carry it down to them.

title: Cairbre and ten set out
summary: Cairbre leads ten men inland from Teallaichean a' Chladaich, reasoning by the coast's own geese, which have not yet gone over in their numbers that autumn, that the crossing season has not yet begun; a household nearer the mountains has scraped its own gatepost clean on the same late reading and by the same error.

title: The eleven do not come home
summary: Cairbre and the ten who went with him fail to reach the valley they set out for and do not return to the shore; no household along the mountains can say it saw them pass, and winter closes the high ground before any search can be made of it that year.

title: Suibhne born at Tobar dhìreach
summary: A son is born to the household that keeps Poit an Teine and the bag of coals, a big child who closes his hand round a finger held out to him and will not readily let it go, so that they say of him he was born holding on; he is given the name Suibhne.

title: Two springs of searching find nothing
summary: The shore and the kin the eleven had set out to help each try the high ground in the spring after they go missing, and again the spring after that, and both times come down with nothing to show for the walking but blistered feet and a country too wide to give up eleven men for the asking.

title: The bones found along the cats' line
summary: A drover's dog worries a length of bone out of the turf off the marked track at the proper close of a crossing season, and searchers over the following days gather a scatter of bone strung along roughly the same course the cats are known to keep, with nothing of what the eleven carried found among it.

title: The eleven buried where they were found
summary: Unable to say with certainty which bones belonged to which man, the southern shore buries the gathered dead together high on the mountain rather than divide them wrongly among separate graves, and keeps alongside Cairbre's name the plainer lesson the country had already made of the matter: that the crossing months keep a count of their own that no household's calendar has yet learned to keep exactly with it.
